clue.text: State where one is sent

parts.note: to be sent is to be carried away in rapture, and this is the dreamlike condition in which that happens

explanation.surface: A question about where a person is dispatched to, as if naming a place or a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks geographical and 'sent' looks like posting someone off; read 'sent' as enraptured instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is enraptured or entranced is in a dazed, hypnotic condition of mind.

clue.text: Church feature or part sent for repair

indicators.note: something sent off to be repaired comes back reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of a church, or a component posted away to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair' rearranges the eight letters of PART SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-arms of a cruciform church building form this architectural feature.

clue.text: Henry Ford, for example?

parts.note: the motor magnate ran his company as an absolute ruler, and was literally a car (auto) man in charge

explanation.surface: A one-line quiz question about the famous American car maker.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as AUTO (car) plus -CRAT (ruler), fitting a car magnate known for running his company with total control.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler; Ford was famously domineering, and the auto prefix nods to his motor cars.

clue.text: Arctic's not right for their cultivation

definitions.text: Arctic's not right for their cultivation

indicators.note: cultivating works the soil over, so the remaining letters are turned over into a new order
not signals that the letter for right is dropped from the frozen region's name

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letters

explanation.surface: Polar conditions are unsuitable for growing desert succulents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from ARCTIC, leaving ACTIC, which 'cultivation' rearranges; the whole clue also describes the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny desert succulents need heat, so a polar climate is plainly wrong for growing them.

clue.text: They were sent mail with outer seal broken

indicators.note: outer says the broken seal's letters go around the outside of the mail
a seal that is broken is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: post is another word for mail

explanation.surface: Someone received letters whose wax seals had been cracked open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes ALES, set outside the mail by 'outer'. The definition plays on the Greek root of the word: one who is sent out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek root means 'one sent out', and the twelve disciples were dispatched to spread the gospel.

clue.text: Stop underling dealing in currency

indicators.note: dealing cards shuffles and redistributes them, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Putting an end to a junior employee's trading in foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing' rearranges all thirteen letters of STOP UNDERLING.
explanation.definitionFit: The full formal name of the British money unit, the pound, is a national currency.

clue.text: Like a planned operation, so captures wrong target

indicators.note: captures means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, as printed after a quoted error

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out incorrectly, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A military plan that seizes the incorrect objective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the target into TRATEG, which the Latin word for so 'captures'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategic move is one forming part of an overall planned campaign.

clue.text: Untidy offspring

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to make a place messy by scattering rubbish
a group of young born to an animal at one birth

explanation.definitionFit: To strew rubbish is to make untidy, and a brood of puppies or kittens is one birth.

clue.text: The point with fish is the smell

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass points
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone insists that the whole issue with fish is how it smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul odour, a particularly unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Furious with loss of father — it's grotesque

indicators.note: losing the father means his abbreviation is taken away from the word

parts.note: frantic means wild or furious
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A man is enraged at losing his father, and the scene is bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove FR from FRANTIC to leave the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, antic means absurd or grotesque, like the capers of a clown.

clue.text: French maid worked better with a little money

parts.note: the sou was a French coin of small value

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A maid from France performed better after a small tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' makes BRETTE; the sou was a small French coin. A soubrette is the stock pert maid of French comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: In comedy and opera a soubrette is the stock pert lady's maid, often French.

clue.text: Fags care for the elderly?

definitions.meaning: fags is British slang for cigarettes; this is a long-standing British cigarette brand
read literally, a service provided to older people

explanation.walkthrough: Fags is British slang for cigarettes; the name is also the nickname of the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic British brand of cigarettes, and also, read whimsically, help offered to pensioners.

clue.text: Cut up at being forcibly treated

definitions.meaning: detained in hospital under the Mental Health Act, in British usage

explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. In Britain a patient detained under a section of the Mental Health Act is said to be sectioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided into sections; in Britain, also compulsorily detained under a section of the mental health law.

clue.text: Corrupt ethic of one taking excessive tea breaks?

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker with a bad attitude who keeps stopping for a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges ETHIC; the rare word names someone addicted to tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theic is a person who drinks too much tea, with the question mark admitting the stretch.

clue.text: Veggie mess discovered at end of motorway in Sussex

definitions.meaning: a vegetable mush or stew, mess being an old word for a dish of food

definitions.text: discovered at end of motorway in Sussex
definitions.meaning: a village at the southern end of the M23 in Sussex, an English county

explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county in southern England; the M23 runs from London towards Brighton and stops near this village.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick porridge of dried peas, and also a Sussex village where the M23 motorway ends.

clue.text: Named after animal swallowed by another back to front

indicators.note: swallowed by means the first animal goes inside the second
back to front means the last letter is moved round to the start

parts.note: another animal, here the mouse
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: Something whose name came from a creature eaten by a different one that was facing backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the other animal's final E to its start, giving EMOUS, which the pony is 'swallowed by'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponymous thing is named after a person, like a title character giving a work its name.

clue.text: Wonders at distance travelled without vehicle upset

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a journey's distance is measured in miles

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the letters run upwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how far they travelled after their car overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'upset' turns the vehicle up into RAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Miracles are marvellous events, things that are wonders.

clue.text: No stains made by wankers

indicators.note: made means formed or produced, so the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A crude claim that some men leave the sheets clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges NO STAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Onanism is masturbation, so those who practise it are, in British slang, wankers.

clue.text: Turn out of building for one to make it tighter

indicators.note: out of, with for, means one letter is taken out of the word and another put in its place

parts.note: construction is a building, or the act of building
U, as in U-turn
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone wants a bend removed from a building so as to tighten it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' is U, as in U-turn; 'out of' and 'for' swap that U for I, one.
explanation.definitionFit: A constriction is a narrowing or tightening, the act of squeezing something in.

clue.text: Boy writer like gay girl

parts.note: Les is a boy's name, short for Leslie
Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A young man who writes is compared to a lesbian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is a pen, and BIC is the familiar ballpoint brand.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective meaning lesbian, relating to women attracted to women.

clue.text: Among library books to lend and not returned

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Some volumes kept for borrowing have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across bookS TO LENd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stolen is taken and never given back, so it is not returned.

clue.text: What guard doesn't begin to control?

definitions.text: What guard doesn't begin to control?

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A riddle about a sentry's job.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of SENTRY; the whole clue also says what a sentry regulates.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard controls the way in to a place, its point of access.

clue.text: Cause a rumpus and threaten sound chastisement

parts.note: to raise a weapon is to threaten with it

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than read, so its spelling changes

parts.note: a cane is used for corporal punishment

explanation.surface: Someone causes trouble by brandishing a stick for punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Raising the cane threatens a beating; 'sound' gives the biblical brother's name instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to make a loud fuss or create an uproar.

clue.text: It's taken in at school, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is heard spoken, not read

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public (private) school

explanation.surface: Something is absorbed at school, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is consumed is taken in, swallowed into the body.

clue.text: Unpaid debt rolling and swelling

parts.note: a bill is a sum owed
owing means still to be paid

explanation.surface: An outstanding bill keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Billowing clouds or sails roll and swell outward in great waves.

clue.text: Counts reports

definitions.meaning: relates or informs, as in telling a story

explanation.definitionFit: To tell can mean to count (as in telling votes) or to relate something.

clue.text: Case of dog, part terrier

parts.note: canis is Latin for dog, the genus name

indicators.note: part means only a piece of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A legal case involving a mixed-breed dog.
explanation.walkthrough: CANIS is Latin for dog; 'part' takes the opening of terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a container, a case for holding tea, film or gas.

clue.text: Layabout is showing knowledge of Greek

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: An idle person proves to know some Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layabout' splits into Lay (a song) and about (reversal).
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is the Greek word for knowledge, especially spiritual insight.
